correctness.rationale: Every proper three-edge-colouring of the 27-edge Pappus graph is covered by recursive edge assignment (120 states); independent matching-decomposition enumeration gives 42 one-factors and the same 120 states. Both algorithms construct all bichromatic connected components, all 324 switch edges, all 20 palette-quotient vertices and their 36 quotient edges, and all 120 shortest-path profiles. Both outputs equal the embedded adjacency certificate. Each quotient component is a ten-vertex universal-vertex join of three disjoint triangles. An explicit base-graph automorphism exchanges the two named sectors. The sign product over one incidence side reverses under each cycle switch, yielding bipartiteness. No extrapolation from small subcases is used.

originality.rationale: The cited 2012 paper and later 2021 exhaustive census treat counts of edge-Kempe equivalence classes; Belcastro and Haas (2017) examine the exact edge-Kempe reconfiguration graphs of cubic graphs in general and examples other than Pappus. The two-class count may follow from the 2021 dataset and is not counted as new. The proposed exact quotient adjacency (two K1 joins with 3 triangles), the named-sector isomorphism, complete diameter-four metric and sphere counts are not reported in the inspected complete accessible texts or targeted search results. The genuinely residual issue is an unindexed prior computation, not an established covering statement.
residual_risks: Belcastro–Haas 2017 develops graph structure; exact Pappus values might be derivable by additional computation but are not implied by its stated general results or examples.
An unindexed historical Pappus graph computational table or a database export could contain an equivalent quotient or metric classification.
Global colour-name quotients must suppress self-loop palette swaps; alternate conventions can report different edge counts.

value.rationale: For the canonical cubic symmetric Pappus Levi graph, optimal Tait colourings split into two transformation sectors. The theorem identifies their complete, unexpectedly small quotient geometry as tetrahedral windmills and their nontrivial bipartite sixty-state lifts with sharp all-source radius and diameter. This answers a natural local-reconfiguration question not answered by a class count alone, providing useful exact benchmark geometry rather than arbitrary decimal statistics.
